---
title: "Point merge"
description: "How OPDI finds the sequencing legs of point merge arrival procedures (pms-leg-entry, pms-leg-exit) and the passage of the merge point (pms-merge-point)."
---

## In one sentence

A **point merge system** is an arrival procedure in which aircraft fly along
an arc, called a sequencing leg, at a nearly constant distance from a merge
point until they are sent directly to it; OPDI publishes the entry and exit of
each leg and the passage of the merge point.

## What it needs

- A table of point merge systems kept with the pipeline: one row per merge
  point, with its coordinates, the distance band and levels of its legs and
  the dates it has been in use (136 merge points at 61 airports).
- An arrival at one of these airports (the destination of the flight list),
  with positions within 60 NM of a merge point.

## How it is computed

1. **Candidates.** Keep the reports within 60 NM of one of the airport's merge
   points and at or below 25,000 ft; compute the distance and the bearing to
   the merge point.
2. **On a leg.** A report is on a leg when, over a 90 s window centred on it:
   - the distance to the merge point varies by at most 1.5 NM;
   - the mean distance lies within the listed band of leg distances, give or
     take 2 NM;
   - the bearing from the merge point turns by at least 8° (the aircraft
     moves around the merge point);
   - at least 80% of the reports have a ground track 60° to 120° off the
     bearing to the merge point (moving along the arc, not towards it).
3. **Leg.** Consecutive reports on a leg form a run. Two runs of one merge
   point at most 120 s apart, turning the same way about it, are one leg. The
   exit is moved forward report by report while the aircraft still moves
   along the arc and stays within 0.5 NM of the distance of the last accepted
   report.
4. **Keep the leg** when it lasts at least 90 s, ends at least 6 NM from the
   merge point, and the aircraft then comes within 3 NM of the merge point
   within 600 s. A leg shorter than 180 s must turn with the arc (a heading
   change of at least 30% of its bearing sweep), and no leg may climb more than
   500 ft from entry to exit.
5. **Direct.** `info.direct_aligned` records whether the aircraft then flew
   straight to the merge point (ground track within 5° of the bearing for at
   least 60 s); it does not decide whether the leg is kept.
6. **Merge point.** `pms-merge-point` is placed at the closest approach to a
   merge point within 3 NM, once per approach, only after every take-off of
   the track, descending or level (at most 500 ft/min of climb), at 150 kt or
   more, and, where the system's name and the landing say which, for a system
   that serves the runway landed on (within 30°).

Nothing is computed across a reception gap kept inside a track.

## Based on

- Developed for OPDI. A point merge system is a merge point with sequencing
  legs at a constant distance from it, which aircraft leave on a
  "direct-to" the merge point ([EUROCONTROL](../resources.qmd#ref-point-merge)); the rule looks
  for exactly that.
- Comparable to the point merge detection of the [`traffic`](../resources.qmd#ref-olive-2019)
  library (`PointMerge`), which also looks for more than 90 s at a nearly
  constant distance from a known merge point followed by a flight towards
  it. OPDI also requires the aircraft to move along the arc, within the
  published band of leg distances, and adds the checks of step 4.
- The merge points and leg dimensions come from published navigation data
  and the [EUROCONTROL Point Merge catalogue](../resources.qmd#ref-pms-catalogue) (each row of
  the table names its source).
- Study: [Holding, point merge and FIR crossings as flight events](../../papers/airspace-events-v1/index.html).

## What is published

Event types `pms-leg-entry`, `pms-leg-exit` and `pms-merge-point`, with
position, altitude, `distance_flown_nm` and `time_passed_s`. The two leg
events carry in `info`: `apt_icao`, `pms_id`, `merge_point`, `leg_seq`,
`direction` (`cw` or `ccw`), `leg_distance_nm`, `leg_level_ft`, `duration_s`,
`distance_nm`, `direct_to_distance_nm` and `direct_aligned`;
`pms-merge-point` carries `apt_icao`, `pms_id`, `merge_point`, `closest_nm`
and `via_leg` (see the [Data dictionary](../data/dictionary.qmd#info-fields)).

Three measurements are set on `pms-leg-exit` only:

| Measurement | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `pms_leg_time_s` | Time on the leg, in seconds. |
| `pms_leg_distance_nm` | Distance flown along the leg, in NM. |
| `pms_direct_to_distance_nm` | Distance to the merge point when the aircraft left the leg, in NM. |

## Use cases

- **Delay absorbed on the legs** per airport and hour: the sum of
  `pms_leg_time_s`.
- **Share of arrivals sent direct** without flying a leg: `pms-merge-point`
  with `info.via_leg` false, against those with a leg.
- **Path stretching**: `pms_leg_distance_nm` per arrival, by entry leg.

## Limitations

Only the airports in the table are examined, and a leg cut by a reception
gap can be missed. See
[Limitations: point merge](../limitations.qmd#lim-point-merge).
